newsitem.title: BRAZIL: New Brazil corp law helps govt, owners - analysts.
newsitem.headline: New Brazil corp law helps govt, owners - analysts.

text.p: Brazilian privatizations will get a boost and company owners will benefit, but minority shareholders lose rights under a new corporate law approved by Congress, analysts said.
"It's good for the government, both federal and state, and good for controllers of companies," said Rodrigo Fiaes, the head of research at local investment bank Banco Icatu.
"They'll have greater flexibility in reorganizing companies. For the federal and state governments, they will be able to absorb all of the premiums paid for privatized companies," he added.

But minority shareholders are stripped of some rights and only partially compensated by the legislation, which was approved by Brazil's Senate last week and is awaiting President Fernando Henrique Cardoso's signature to become law.

Under the law, minority shareholders will lose the right to offer their stock at market or book value if a company is transferred, scrapping a requirement that the new owner extend the same buying price to minority holders.

Analysts said the change means investors will be able to offer larger sums for the controlling stakes because they will not have set aside any funds to buy additional stakes from minority shareholders.
A clause in the new law would compensate minority holders of preferred shares with a 10 percent dividend premium, but "I don't think that's enough," a local analyst said.
Under prior legislation, preferred shareholders only had the guarantee of being paid their dividends before common stock holders.
Analysts said the real intent of the new law is to smooth the road for upcoming mega-privatizations.
"This law was designed to facilitate the privatizations in the telecommunications and electrical sectors," said one local bank analyst.
Prior to their privatizations, some firms will be split into smaller unit while others will have their subsidiaries grouped into regional companies.

Brazil expects to raise more than $10 billion this year and even more in 1998 from the sale of state miner Cia Vale do Rio Doce, federal power holding Eletrobras and federal telecoms Telebras and a host of other assets.
